learning_objectives.en: Apply so/too/either/neither accurately and complete an unseen exam-style text.
learning_objectives.vi: Dùng so/too/either/neither chính xác rồi luyện bài đọc kiểu thi.

content.en: For positive clauses, use “So + auxiliary + subject” or “subject + auxiliary + too”. For negative clauses, use “Neither + auxiliary + subject” or “subject + negative auxiliary + either”. Match the tense.
content.vi: Với câu khẳng định: So + trợ động từ + chủ ngữ hoặc chủ ngữ + trợ động từ + too. Với câu phủ định: Neither + trợ động từ + chủ ngữ hoặc chủ ngữ + trợ động từ phủ định + either. Giữ đúng thì.

vocabulary.example_en: Saving water is a practical measure.
vocabulary.example_vi: Tiết kiệm nước là biện pháp thực tế.

vocabulary.example_en: A long-term solution needs reliable evidence.
vocabulary.example_vi: Giải pháp dài hạn cần bằng chứng đáng tin.

vocabulary.example_en: I agree with this argument to some extent.
vocabulary.example_vi: Tôi đồng ý với lập luận này ở một mức độ nào đó.

vocabulary.example_en: On the other hand, the project requires funding.
vocabulary.example_vi: Mặt khác, dự án cần kinh phí.

grammar.title: so / too / either / neither
grammar.form: So do I. / I do too. / Neither do I. / I do not either.

explanation.en: Do not combine neither with not. The auxiliary changes with the original tense.
explanation.vi: Không dùng neither với not; trợ động từ thay đổi theo thì câu gốc.

grammar.example: A: I enjoy wildlife documentaries. B: So do I. / A: I do not like littering. B: Neither do I.

strategies.en: For NG, do not infer facts from background knowledge. For summary gaps, check lexical and grammar fit.
strategies.vi: Với NG không suy diễn theo kiến thức ngoài; với summary gap soát cả nghĩa lẫn ngữ pháp.

reason.vi: Neither đã mang nghĩa phủ định.

mini_review.en: Do I know the difference between “Neither do I” and “I do not either”?
mini_review.vi: Tôi hiểu sự khác biệt giữa Neither do I và I do not either chưa?

passages.title: A pocket wildlife garden: the evidence after two years (fictional Bellmere trial)
passages.text:
[A] When the fictional town of Bellmere proposed replacing an old car park with a small wildlife garden, some residents immediately called it a waste of public money. Others believed that even a modest patch of greenery could improve the town. The council invited ecologists, shop owners and families to review a two-year trial before making a permanent decision.

[B] During the first spring, volunteers planted flowering species native to the region and left narrow strips of grass uncut. By July, monthly observations recorded nineteen kinds of visiting pollinators, compared with eight in the first survey. The researchers emphasised that these numbers did not prove the garden had caused the change: temperatures and observation hours had also varied between the surveys.

[C] A nearby café owner argued that the project attracted more visitors, although the council had not collected reliable information about customer spending. Several parents welcomed the benches and shaded path, while two residents complained that the garden looked untidy. The researchers suggested keeping some open grass near the entrance but warned against using chemical sprays just to create a perfectly neat appearance.

[D] In the second summer, unusually dry weather damaged a number of new plants. The council replaced them with species better suited to low rainfall and installed a rainwater collection tank. The ecologists recommended measuring the garden for at least five years before judging its long-term ecological impact. In their view, the most sensible policy was to continue collecting evidence rather than claiming either immediate success or total failure.

[E] The final trial report recommended keeping the wildlife garden and adding signs to explain why dead leaves and fallen branches sometimes remain in place. It also proposed a monthly volunteer day for local schools. The report did not say whether house prices nearby had increased. Instead, it called for future surveys that would separate environmental outcomes from social and economic effects.

instruction.en: Complete the reply with the best expression.
instruction.vi: Hoàn thành phản hồi bằng cách tự nhiên nhất.

questions.prompt_en: A: I care about forest protection. B: ______. (so)
questions.prompt_vi: A: Tôi quan tâm bảo vệ rừng. B: ______ (so)
questions.explanation_vi: Câu hiện tại đơn khẳng định cần do.

questions.prompt_en: A: I do not support hunting endangered animals. B: ______. (neither)
questions.prompt_vi: A: Tôi không ủng hộ săn loài nguy cấp. B: ______ (neither)
questions.explanation_vi: Neither tự mang nghĩa phủ định.

questions.prompt_en: A: I visited a nature reserve last month. B: ______. (too)
questions.prompt_vi: A: Tháng trước tôi thăm khu bảo tồn. B: ______ (too)
questions.explanation_en: Past simple changes the auxiliary to did.

questions.prompt_en: A: I have never visited a zoo. B: ______. (either)
questions.prompt_vi: A: Tôi chưa từng đến vườn thú. B: ______ (either)
questions.explanation_en: Present perfect negative needs have not.
questions.explanation_vi: Hiện tại hoàn thành phủ định cần have not.

questions.prompt_en: A: I am worried about plastic waste. B: ______. (so)
questions.prompt_vi: A: Tôi lo rác nhựa. B: ______ (so)
questions.explanation_en: With be, invert the same be form.
questions.explanation_vi: Với be, đảo am trước chủ ngữ.

questions.prompt_en: A: They cannot attend the clean-up. B: ______. (neither)
questions.prompt_vi: A: Họ không thể dự buổi dọn rác. B: ______ (neither)
questions.explanation_vi: Giữ modal can theo câu gốc.
